1. In the space provided, write a “F” if the statement describes frictional unemployment, “ST” for structural
unemployment, “C” for cyclical unemployment.

 a. Fred Flintstone was laid off from the rock quarry as the industry has slowed down because
     the country is suffering from a recession.                                        _____________

 b. Ronald McDonald, who just graduated from Clown School, is looking for, and hasn’t yet
    found his first job.                                                          _____________

 c. Thomas the diesel train engineer is expecting to be out of work shortly, as diesel trains are
    being replaced with electric trains. Thomas doesn’t know anything about electric trains.   _____________

 d. Paul lost his job as a banker because the finance company he works for has just closed
   down because of the recent financial crisis.                                       _____________

 e. Colonel Saunders was laid off from his cooking job at KFC, since people are eating less
     fried chicken. Fortunately, he is a skilled cook and can find a new job.                 _____________

 f. Mickey Mouse voluntarily quit his position at Disney & has decided that he will seek a
   new career as a rock music singer instead.                                       _____________

 g. Bob the Builder found out that he was let go from his job as the housing market has
    crashed following last year’s stock market crash.                                  _____________

 h. Snoopy is looking for a job during the summer, since school is closed until September.    _____________

 i. Luke Skywalker has just moved his residence to Dagobah, and is looking for work there.   _____________

 j. Ms Strawberry Shortcake usually works picking fruits, but she cannot find any work
    because climate change has made the region unsuitable for fruit farms.                 _____________

2. In 1992, the minimum wage in New Jersey increased from $4.25 to $5.05 per hour (an 18.8% increase), while
in the adjacent state of Pennsylvania it remained at $4.25. In their 1994 study, "Minimum Wages and
Employment: A Case Study of the Fast-Food Industry in New Jersey and Pennsylvania", David Card and Alan
Krueger gathered data from fast food restaurants near the New Jersey / Pennsylvania border, before and after the
minimum wage increase, to see what effect the increase had on employment in New Jersey. Surprisingly, they
found that the increase in the minimum wage slightly increased employment in the New Jersey restaurants.
